name: Ashwall ForgeWarden Split-Apron & Sleeves Kit
description:
A heavy split-leg forge apron in charred split-grain synthetic leather — deep brown-black with a surface texture of small overlapping scales pressed into the hide during tanning. The bib reaches mid-chest, secured by adjustable neck and waist straps with quick-release buckles. Matched detachable sleeves run from wrist to upper arm, fastening to a shoulder yoke with industrial snap rings. All edges are double-stitched in heat-resistant aramid thread.

The apron's interior is lined with a thin ceramic-fiber batting that insulates against radiant heat from forge and plasma-arc work. Burn marks, weld spatter scars, and grease stains are universal on worn units — a clean kit reads as brand new or desk-bought.
functionality: Rated for radiant heat, weld spatter, and minor plasma arc flash. Split-leg design allows full leg mobility. Detachable sleeves can be added or removed without removing the apron. Quick-release buckles allow emergency doffing in under four seconds.
what_it_says: You work hot, you work hands-on, and you've got the scars to prove you know what you're doing.
worn_by: blacksmiths and bladesmiths in Shelf craft shops
story_hooks: An old apron in a secondhand stall has a name stamped into the bib leather — it belongs to a forge worker who died in a plant fire six months ago, officially ruled an accident.
A batch of ForgeWarden kits was manufactured with ceramic liner batting that's 40% thinner than spec — someone at Ashwall signed off on the substitution.
A master welder refuses to break in a new apron, insisting her twenty-year-old unit carries luck — someone wants it badly enough to offer three times its value.
